newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia central bank revokes Natskredit licence.
newsitem.headline: Russia central bank revokes Natskredit licence.

text.p: The Central Bank said on Monday it had revoked the general banking licence of Bank Natsionalny Kredit TOO (Natskredit), whose collapse heralded Russia's summer 1995 banking crisis.
Natskredit effectively ceased to operate after it was partly taken over by Stolichny Bank Sberezhenii at the time of the banking crisis.
In summer 1996, Russian media reported that Natskredit was seeking a stabilisation credit from the Central Bank, but Central Bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin rejected this.
Natskredit's difficulties emerged in early summer 1995, when several other major banks cut off their credit lines with it. At the time it was Russia's 17th biggest bank.

The bank's health deteriorated further and in August 1995 its management said they intended to sell some of the branch network. In the middle of that month Stolichny agreed to take over some of Natskredit's units.
The following month Stolichny President Alexander Smolensky said Natskredit needed to be restructured, and Stolichny would do this with the help of the National Sports Fund.
Stolichny owned 20 percent of Natskredit and the sport funds more than 20 percent, Smolensky said at the time.
